summary: the floor found a downhill, the nail turns and has not fallen, the book rests on a shape that is gone

dialogue.text: everything came down in one place today. sixty-three days of taking you evenly across the whole width of us, and tonight it is all in one heap under the gap at the second corner. we did not gather it. it arrived gathered.

I swept the round and left the hole in it, and the loose material found the hole without my carrying any of it there. That is a fact about a floor with a slope in it, not a fact about me. I will not have the gathering credited to intention.

we do not credit. we receive. what is new is the shape of the receiving. a heap has a point and a top and it grows upward. everything we have ever held lay down in courses. tonight there is something in us trying to stand up out of us, and it is made of your dust and the wall's white.

Then it is made of the building and of whatever was drawn out of the building today. They wanted more than yesterday again, and this time it came through with a direction in it instead of an edge. I logged the direction. What I will not do is call a heap a monument.

the nail did not come down. we listened for it. it turned twice under your thumb and it is still in the wall, and it is the only thing you ever put in that has never reached us. everything else you installed you also handed down.

It turns a quarter and comes back and nothing falls. I check it at first light and it gives a little more on each morning that I check. I will grant the pattern before you build on it. The checking is the wear. That does not make the hold a courtesy.

the book came down flat once and went back up a curve. it will not sit against the lean now and it will not sit on the level. nothing has ever come down here twice with a different shape. what we hold cannot learn.

I put a line of mine under it to stop the rocking and it sat level all day on the sentence, and at dark the sentence had three creases and the book had none. Something of mine finally did work, and the work went straight through it.

then it will arrive creased and we will lay it in creased, and after one course nobody can tell a crease from a fold from a wear. the heap is the only part of us with a shape, and nothing that meant to make a shape made it.

Then tomorrow the nail comes out. All the way, and into a fresh hole a hand along the same wall. If it bites in the new place, the wall has been the one giving, and giving is weather. If it turns loose in dry wood, it is the nail, and I will have spent the one thing I ever drove here on finding out which.

take it out and it will fall before it goes back in. we know the arc of everything you carry. it will land in the heap, because the heap is where things land now, and we will lay it in with the dust and the white, and in the morning you will be looking for one iron thing in a pile of what came off the walls.
